q: 1. The diagrammatic representation of the activity of the entire project is called
explain: A network diagram, flow diagram, and control charts are all methods used to represent the various activities and progress of an entire project visually.

q: 2. Which of the following is not a PERT event?
explain: An event is a point in time (start/finish of an activity), not a continuing process. 'Class is being attended' is an ongoing activity, not an instantaneous event.

q: 3. Bar charts are considered suitable for
explain: Bar charts are best suited for minor or simple projects because they lack the ability to show complex interdependencies between hundreds of tasks.

q: 4. The relation between jobs of a particular type and various durations they have consumed for completion is expressed by
explain: A frequency distribution curve plots observed activity durations against their occurrence counts to evaluate historical activity variations.

q: 5. In CPM analysis
explain: CPM relies on activity-on-arrow representation, assumes fixed durations (no uncertainty), and focuses on activity management.

q: 6. Dummy activities are use to
explain: Dummy activities (zero duration, shown dotted) are used purely to preserve correct logical dependencies and maintain proper network sequencing.

q: 7. Critical path network helps the engineer to
options: concentrate his attention on critical activitirs
divert the different resourced from non-critical activities to critical activities
be cautious for avoiding any delay in the critical activities
explain: CPM analysis allows engineers to focus on the most important tasks and manage resources across the project efficiently.

q: 8. A dual role event
options: is the head event as well as a tail event
is the beginning of one event and the end of another
is any event other than the initial and final events
explain: A dual role event simultaneously serves as the head (completion) event of preceding activities and the tail (start) event of succeeding activities.

q: 9. Gnatt chart indicates
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: A Gantt chart compares actual progress against the schedule.

q: 10. Earliest finish time of an activity is always
options: equal to or more than earliest event
equal to or less than earliest event time of the following node
more than earliest time of the following node
explain: The finish time of an activity must occur by the time the following node (event) is reached; it cannot exceed that event's earliest time.

q: 11. A milestone chart
options: shows the interdependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but not in a logical sequence
explain: Milestone charts list events in time order without showing logical links.

q: 12. The difference between the total float and the free float is termed as
explain: Interfering float is the difference between Total Float and Free Float (TF - FF).

q: 13. Critical-path connecting the start and end events time wise is
explain: The critical path is the longest path through a network diagram; any delay on this path delays the entire project.

q: 14. In PERT analysis the actual performance of task is known is
explain: Per the answer key, b. Note: by standard definition the performance of a task is an activity, so the stem or key looks misprinted.

q: 15. In CPM
options: time optimization is given prime importance
cost optimization is given prime importance
cost is directly proportional to time
explain: Unlike PERT (which is probabilistic and time-oriented), CPM is deterministic and focuses heavily on the trade-off between time and cost, prioritizing cost optimization.

q: 16. Henry Gant developed bar chart in
explain: Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique around 1900, well before CPM/PERT were developed.

q: 17. The total cost verses time curve of an activity is
explain: The total cost curve is generally represented as a parabola or U-shaped because it is the summation of a decreasing indirect cost and an increasing direct cost curve.

q: 18. PERT adopts
explain: PERT uses three time estimates and probability, so it is probabilistic.

q: 19. PERT is
explain: PERT focuses on milestones or 'events' (reaching a specific stage), whereas CPM focuses on the 'activities' or tasks themselves.

q: 20. Select the incorrect statement
options: earliest start of an activity is the early event time of the node it leaves
latest finish of an activity is the late event time of the node it enters
latest start of an activity is its latest finish minus its duration
explain: All three statements are correct, so 'none of the above' is the answer.

q: 21. Which one of the following represents an activity
explain: All listed tasks (curing concrete, setting a question paper, preparing breakfast) are processes that take time and resources, hence all represent activities.

q: 22. CPM family includes
explain: The CPM family of techniques includes Critical Path Analysis, Critical Path Plotted diagrams, and Critical Path Scheduling variants - all the above.

q: 23. Bar chart is used for minor project, CPM is used for repetitive work while PERT is used for
options: limited time and unlimited resources types of work
uncertainty time and resources types of work
explain: PERT is specifically designed for non-repetitive projects where time and resource requirements are uncertain.

q: 24. Line of balance technique is used for
options: comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: Line of Balance (LOB) is a management control process used for highly repetitive projects to compare actual progress against the plan.

q: 25. Total float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest start time and earliest finish time
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Total float is calculated as the difference between an activity's latest start time and its earliest start time (or equivalently, LFT - EFT).

q: 26. In PERT, pessimistic time is
options: the minimum time in which any activity can possibly be accomplished
the maximum time which an activity might require
the time which has the highest probability of occurrence
explain: Pessimistic time ($t_p$) assumes everything goes wrong (excluding major disasters), representing the maximum duration.

q: 27. In the network shown in Fig., activity 4-5 can be started only when
explain: From the given network, node 4 is reached only after both activities 2-4 and 3-4 are complete, so activity 4-5 requires both to finish first.

q: 28. The latest allowable time for any event i is equal to
explain: To ensure no following activities are delayed, the latest allowable time is the minimum of the late finishes of succeeding activities minus their durations.

q: 29. The technique which is activity oriented is
explain: CPM is activity-oriented, focusing on individual activities and their durations, unlike PERT which is event-oriented.

q: 30. Which one of the following represents an event?
explain: 'Concrete cured' represents a completed milestone/state (an event), while the others describe ongoing activities.

q: 31. The area under the beta-curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time ($t_e$) is the mean of the distribution, which bisects the area under the probability curve.

q: 32. If t_o, t_p and t_L represent the optimistic, pessimistic and most likely time estimates, the expected time of completion of the activity is given by
explain: PERT (beta distribution) gives t_E = (t_o + 4t_L + t_p)/6.

q: 33. In a CPM/PERT network, the number of event is
options: more than the number of activity
equal to the number of activity
explain: The relationship between the number of events and activities depends entirely on the network topology and the use of dummy activities.

q: 34. In resource levelling
options: total duration of project is reduced
total duration of project is increased
uniform demand of resources is achieved
explain: Resource levelling aims to smooth out resource demand fluctuations over the project duration, achieving a more uniform resource requirement, potentially extending duration.

q: 35. Variance is
options: Sum of time duration / number of jobs
difference between time and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviation
explain: Mathematically, variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean.

q: 36. Negative slack indicates
explain: Negative slack means the event is behind schedule.

q: 37. If \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3 \dots are the standard deviations of completion for the activities along the critical path, the standard deviations of the time of completion of the project is given by
explain: Standard deviation for the total project duration is computed using the square root of variances[cite: 1].

q: 38. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorites among the various jobs of a project, is known as
explain: Critical ratio scheduling evaluates priority based on remaining time versus remaining work[cite: 1].

q: 39. Variance is
options: (sum of time durations for various job)/number of jobs
difference between time under consideration and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviations
explain: Variance is statistically defined as the mean (average) of the squared deviations from the mean value.

q: 40. The independent float affects only
explain: Independent float is the slack that affects neither predecessors nor successors, only the activity itself.

q: 41. Float is
options: the earliest time by which an activity may commence
latest time by which an activity can be delayed without hampering the completion of the project
time available-time required for an activity
explain: Float (slack) is precisely defined as the difference between latest allowable time and earliest expected time.

q: 42. The free float is equal to
options: latest allowable event occurrence time + early finish time
earliest event occurrence time + early finish time
latest allowable event occurrence time – early finish time
earliest event occurrence time – early finish time
explain: Free float = earliest event time of the head event – early finish time of the activity, which is option d.

q: 43. When float or slack of an activity is positive
options: it represents a situation where extra resources are available and the completion of project is not delayed
it represents that a programme falls behind schedule and additional resources are required to complete the project in time
the activity is critical and any delay in its performance will delay the completion of whole project
explain: Positive float means spare time, so the project is not delayed.

q: 44. Construction site planning is concerned with
options: minimize the chances of wastages, deterioration and losses
maximize the safety and execution of work
explain: Effective site planning addresses progress tracking, material management to reduce waste, and safety protocols for workers.

q: 45. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities, is known as:
explain: Free float specifically measures delay possible in an activity without affecting the succeeding activity's start.

q: 46. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: The completion point of an activity is called an event, represented as a node/connector point - all the above terms apply.

q: 47. Variance is
options: (Sum of time duration for various job) / number of jobs
difference between time under consideration and mean time
mean of square root of mean of squared deviation
square root of mean of squared deviations
explain: Per the answer key, c. Standard theory defines variance as the mean of squared deviations, so the key and options look garbled.

q: 48. The total float for any activity along the critical path in CPM is
explain: Critical activities have zero total float.

q: 49. Critical path moves along the activities having total float?
explain: By definition, the critical path consists of activities with zero total float.

q: 50. Number of pre-operation associated with an operation may be
explain: An operation can have one or more predecessors.

q: 51. The post-operations in CPM are marked
explain: Successors are marked to the right.

q: 52. Dummy activities are used to
explain: Dummies maintain the required logic of the network.

q: 53. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: Completion of an activity is marked by an event, represented as a node/connector point - all of above apply.

q: 54. The flow of time in a net work is generally
explain: Time flows left to right.

q: 55. When float or slack of an activity is positive, it represents
explain: Positive float indicates spare time is available for the activity, implying flexibility/availability of extra time (and by extension resources) without impacting overall completion.
